state.project: logos-sort: a distribution-aware adaptive numeric sort engine in C. Thesis: addressing beats comparing -- detect structure (cardinality, sortedness, skew, quantization) and dispatch to a zero- or low-comparison path instead of a comparison sort.
state.hardware: i9-13900H, 6 performance cores + 8 efficient cores, 14 bench threads, WSL2. Single socket.

method.paired_ab: two variants run adjacently on the two halves of one array, order alternated; median of the ratio with p10/p90. Drift cancels inside a pair, ordering bias across pairs.
method.resolving_floor: the same engine on both sides reads 1.000; 40 pairs resolve ~3.7% at 8M and ~6.1% at 1M. An effect below that is not a result.
method.layout_bias: engine copies differing only in renamed symbols differ up to 1.24x from code alignment, so any claim under 1.25x needs the copy assignment permuted or the mechanism traced.
method.verification: every benchmark checks output against a reference; ~45,899 harness property checks.
method.calibration_line: memcpy 64MB and std::sort 1M are printed per run; quiet is ~2.9ms/~65ms. A loaded box flatters logos, because barrier-heavy opponents lose more to preemption.

state.competitive_position: At 14 threads on AVX2 hardware: parity with x86-simd-sort on random shapes (0.86-1.08x), ahead on structured (few_distinct 1.4x, quantized 1.76x, block shapes 2.2-2.5x). Loses to AVX-512 x86-simd-sort on all unstructured shapes. Loses 2-9x to std::sort below ~100 elements.
state.memory: Peak heap of one cold call, bytes per element at 10M, one thread: logos 15.7, LSD radix 16.0, timsort 3.9, IPS4o 0.2, std::sort 0.0, x86-simd-sort 0.0, logos strict in-place entry 0.0.

Q_SZ_networks.instructions: Branchless Batcher sorting networks for 4-16 elements replacing insertion sort in the leaf. Rate the speedup on RANDOM calls at n=16, one thread.

Q_SZ_net4.instructions: The same networks, rated on RANDOM calls at n=4.

Q_SZ_latqueue.instructions: The lattice map phase claiming chunks from a counter instead of equal slices, at 14 threads on quantized. Rate the speedup.

Q_SZ_tiles.instructions: The same work queue applied to relocation's memcpy output tiles, 14 threads. Rate it.

Q_SZ_prescan.instructions: Making the dispatcher's prescan compare with vectors (AVX2 blocks of 32) where its block loop had compiled to sixteen scalar compares and a serial OR chain. Rate it on SORTED input.

Q_SZ_kink.instructions: Swapping a kinked adjacent pair back where it stands inside a run (Reidemeister I), on sorted blocks with 0.1% kinks at one thread. Rate it.

Q_SZ_datestr.instructions: Parsing fixed-width ISO-8601 timestamps to a numeric key and using argsort + one gather, against std::sort on std::string. Rate it.

Q_SZ_datenum.instructions: Telling the sort the origin and step of NUMERIC epoch-millisecond timestamps, so it can convert to integer keys and radix only the varying bytes. Rate it against the engine.

Q_SZ_hugepage.instructions: Huge pages for the engine's large buffers, at 14 threads and 8M, with the mechanism verified firing (98MB AnonHugePages vs 0). Rate it.

Q_SZ_gallop.instructions: A galloping two-strand merge for one sparse strand spanning every value over dense blocks, one thread, 8.4M. Rate it.

Q_MECH_lattice_idle.instructions: logos-sort's lattice counting route at 14 threads shows only 8.4 of 14 threads busy on average, with NONE waiting at a barrier and no preemption (cpu/busy = 1.00). Every thread is handed exactly n/P work in both of its parallel phases. Which is the binding constraint?

criteria.serial_merge: the serial merge between the two parallel phases
criteria.table_teardown: freeing the per-thread count tables at the end
criteria.thread_creation: creating and joining the worker threads, paid once per parallel phase
criteria.memory_bandwidth: the emit phase saturating memory bandwidth, so extra threads cannot help
criteria.thread_imbalance: unequal work per thread inside the phases
criteria.cache_pressure: the per-thread tables being too large for L2

Q_MECH_proposal_failure.instructions: An outside sorting proposal arrives for logos-sort. Given that the engine sorts at 0.8-2.1 ns/element at 14 threads and already certifies cardinality, sortedness, skew and quantization from one shared sample, which failure mode will the proposal hit FIRST?

criteria.per_element_cost: its per-element transform costs more than the whole sort
criteria.destroys_order: its transform is not monotone in the value, so the output is not sorted
criteria.already_subsumed: the engine's existing routes already exploit the same structure
criteria.isolated_win_only: the kernel wins in isolation and loses end to end
criteria.gate_never_fires: the branch it relies on fires zero times on its target shape
criteria.fixed_cost_per_call: it is free at scale but adds cost to every small call

Q_MECH_small_end.instructions: logos-sort loses 2-9x to std::sort below ~100 elements. Entering the dispatcher costs ~5.6ns before any work, and psort_f64's stack frame is 42,576 bytes, which stack-clash protection probes a page at a time on EVERY call (11 probes). Which lever recovers the most at n = 2-10?

criteria.thin_front: a small-frame front function, with the large body behind a call
criteria.fewer_gates: skipping more dispatcher gates at tiny n
criteria.nothing: nothing structural; the remaining cost is irreducible

Q_OPEN_O01.instructions: A persistent worker pool replacing per-call pthread_create. Context: The lattice route pays spawn+join twice (map and emit): create+join of 13 workers measures 0.564ms of a 1.597ms emit phase, about 1.13ms of a 6.58ms call. Every pthread_create already goes through par_run/par_spawn, so it is a change to two functions rather than 23 sites. Rate the speedup a paired A/B would measure against the engine as it ships, remembering that the resolving floor is ~3.7% at 8M.

Q_OPEN_O02.instructions: Interleaving the lattice map's keys[] and cnts[] into one 16-byte record. Context: The map is 68% of the route at concurrency 10.72/14. Its hot path touches keys[idx] then cnts[idx] at the same random index in two separate 400KB arrays: two cache lines per element where one record would be one. Caution: the ledger's 'interleaved counters' for the partition histogram measured neutral (0.95-1.04). Rate the speedup a paired A/B would measure against the engine as it ships, remembering that the resolving floor is ~3.7% at 8M.

Q_OPEN_O03.instructions: A thin front for the dispatcher: prescan and insertion sort in a small-frame function, the large body behind a call. Context: psort_f64's frame is 42,576 bytes, so stack-clash protection probes 11 pages on every call including a sort of 2 elements. Entering the dispatcher costs ~5.6ns before any work. Rate the speedup a paired A/B would measure against the engine as it ships, remembering that the resolving floor is ~3.7% at 8M.

Q_OPEN_O04.instructions: An MSD radix for the f64 leaf that stops after the top four key bytes and finishes tie groups by insertion. Context: Measured: on uniform, heavy_tail and int_wide the real tie groups under a 32-bit key prefix hold at most 7-10 elements, and few_distinct/quantized ties are 100% duplicates (free). But clustered collapses to 10,274 and bimodal to 512,897, because the top 32 bits resolve to ~1e-6 of the magnitude inside one binade. Rate the speedup a paired A/B would measure against the engine as it ships, remembering that the resolving floor is ~3.7% at 8M.

Q_OPEN_O05.instructions: Splitting one overlapping chain's merge across threads in relocation's phase 2. Context: Phase 2 is already queue-driven, but one long chain is a single indivisible task, so one thread merges it while thirteen wait at the second barrier. Equalising the output tiles changed nothing (0.96-1.04), which is what points here. Rate the speedup a paired A/B would measure against the engine as it ships, remembering that the resolving floor is ~3.7% at 8M.

Q_OPEN_O06.instructions: Windowing the f64 partition's key grid from trimmed quantiles instead of the raw sample. Context: One zero in the sample is enough to defeat the certificates: a sloped sine starts at 0, a[0] is always sampled, the key grid in total-order key space goes coarse because the neighbourhood of zero spans hundreds of binades, and the grid is rejected. The same wave shifted to its crest runs at 0.85-0.88 of the time. Rate the speedup a paired A/B would measure against the engine as it ships, remembering that the resolving floor is ~3.7% at 8M.

Q_OPEN_O07.instructions: An int32 twin of the short-reach route. Context: The f64 short-reach route (sort index blocks where they lie, repair only the seams) is 1.9-2.5x at one thread and 1.3-1.5x at 14, and weighs 0.10 bytes per element at one thread against 15.5. int32 has no such route, and no relocation either. Rate the speedup a paired A/B would measure against the engine as it ships, remembering that the resolving floor is ~3.7% at 8M.

Q_OPEN_O08.instructions: A GPU/SIMT port of the counting and radix paths. Context: The thesis is that addressing beats comparing; on a CPU the scatter is bound by per-core latency (proved three times: ping-pong removed 37% of traffic for 12% of time, huge pages and streaming stores both measured exactly zero). A GPU is the one hardware where scatter is cheap. Rate the speedup a paired A/B would measure against the engine as it ships, remembering that the resolving floor is ~3.7% at 8M.
criteria: no better than the CPU engine

Q_OPEN_O09.instructions: logos_query: promoting the order/analytics API (rank, select, quantiles, topk, count_in_range, distinct) to first-class entry points. Context: When the deliverable is ORDER or ANALYTICS rather than a sorted array, the no-scatter model already measures quantiles 87x, top-k 7x, range-count 42x against sort-first baselines -- but those baselines were unfair (sort-first and nth_element), and a fair querybench against radix-select and streaming heaps is still owed. Rate the speedup a paired A/B would measure against the engine as it ships, remembering that the resolving floor is ~3.7% at 8M.

Q_OPEN_O10.instructions: A structure-router: probe cheaply, send structured data to logos's counting/lattice paths and everything else to x86-simd-sort wholesale. Context: logos beats x86-simd-sort only on structured data (few_distinct 1.4x, quantized 1.76x, block shapes 2.2-2.5x) and loses on every unstructured shape. The probe is the shared sample, already 1-4% of a call. Rate the speedup a paired A/B would measure against the engine as it ships, remembering that the resolving floor is ~3.7% at 8M.

Q_M_floor.instructions: A benchmark reports a 4% speedup as the median of 40 paired runs. On the same harness, the SAME code on both sides reads 1.000 with a p90 deviation of 8-14% per pair, and 40 pairs resolve about 3.7%. Judge the claim: the 4% is reportable as a result, provided the null is stated alongside it.

criteria.true: The claim holds: 4% is just outside the measured floor, so it is reportable with the null quoted
criteria.false: The claim fails: 4% is inside the noise and needs more pairs or a traced mechanism

Q_M_layout.instructions: Two engine copies built from IDENTICAL source and flags, differing only in renamed symbols, measured up to 1.24x apart on a quiet box, deterministically, because symbol lengths change code alignment. A new A/B now shows 1.15x. Judge the claim: that 1.15x should not be trusted until the variant-to-copy assignment is permuted or the mechanism is traced directly.

criteria.true: The claim holds: below about 1.25x the layout bias can produce the whole effect
criteria.false: The claim fails: 1.15x is large enough to trust as measured

Q_M_trace.instructions: A build instrumented with per-phase tracing (fprintf at each phase boundary) times a phase at 2 ms. Judge the claim: that number must not be used to decide whether the phase is worth optimising.

criteria.true: The claim holds: the trace calls change the whole function's code generation, so such a build says WHICH path ran and what share each phase took, never a price against a normal build
criteria.false: The claim fails: the traced build runs the same code, so its phase timing is usable

Q_M_oracle.instructions: A double-precision sort's output is compared byte-for-byte against libc qsort's output on the same input. Judge the claim: that is NOT a sound correctness oracle.

criteria.true: The claim holds: qsort treats -0.0 and +0.0 as equal, so byte comparison flags correct sorts as wrong; check ascending under < plus the bitwise multiset instead
criteria.false: The claim fails: identical bytes is the strongest available check

Q_M_microbench.instructions: A kernel measures 1.22x faster than the one it replaces, in isolation. Judge the claim: it should not ship until the FULL operation is A/B'd end to end.

criteria.true: The claim holds: in this repo three kernels won in isolation and LOST when integrated
criteria.false: The claim fails: a faster kernel makes the whole faster

Q_M_loaded.instructions: A fair-fight benchmark runs with its calibration line reading 3.5x the quiet reference, and its ratios favour the engine under test. Judge the claim: those ratios are an upper bound rather than a measurement.

criteria.true: The claim holds: barrier-heavy opponents lose more to preemption than chunk-parallel phases do, so a loaded box flatters this engine
criteria.false: The claim fails: every contender ran under the same load, so the ratios hold

Q_M_fallback.instructions: A resource-exhaustion fallback path is written and code-reviewed but has never executed. Judge the claim: it cannot be relied on until it has been forced to run.

criteria.true: The claim holds: injecting failures found 2,215 of 8,316 allocation failures and 154 of 186 thread-creation failures ending in wrong output, a crash or a hang, under thousands of green checks
criteria.false: The claim fails: the code is straightforward and was reviewed

Q_M_stub.instructions: A charting library is replaced by a hand-written stub in tests, and 216 charts pass every test the stub drives. Judge the claim: the rendering is still unverified.

criteria.true: The claim holds: in a real browser a log axis could not be zoomed inside one decade and a pan killed the tab; a fake must reproduce the library's awkward behaviour
criteria.false: The claim fails: 216 charts is thorough coverage

Q_M_precision.instructions: A vendor reports '193.6x faster' with no stated repetition count, measured from laptops. Judge the claim: the figure's four significant digits are not supported by its method.

criteria.true: The claim holds: four significant figures implies about +-0.05%, which an unrepeated laptop measurement cannot support
criteria.false: The claim fails: the figure is simply what they measured

Q_M_statistic.instructions: A routing gate is documented in a comment as reading an inversion rate over about 1900 sampled pairs. Judge the claim: that comment should not be trusted when reasoning about why the gate misfires.

criteria.true: The claim holds: count what the loop actually reads. The same comment here described a loop reading 7 pairs a whole array apart, and it turned away 6 of 7 near-sorted inputs
criteria.false: The claim fails: the comment documents the code's intent and is a fair summary
